description: Lugbara (Lugbarati) is a Central Sudanic language spoken by about two million people in West Nile, around Arua, Koboko, Maracha and Terego, and across the border in north-eastern DR Congo.
notes: Drafted by Claude (AI) for the Lugbara courses (#132) with low confidence in Lugbara; needs a native-speaker review.

why.title: The language of **Arua, Koboko and Mount Wati.**
why.text: Lugbara is a cousin of Madi, Aringa and Logo, a Central Sudanic family that reaches from Uganda into DR Congo and South Sudan. Learn it for family, travel, work, and the songs, dances and stories of West Nile.

cards.title: For family
cards.text: Talk with grandparents and relatives in Arua and Koboko.

cards.title: For travellers
cards.text: Find your way from Arua to Koboko, Nebbi and Mount Wati.

cards.title: For the curious
cards.text: Meet a tonal language with no noun classes and no verb prefixes, built from short words that never change.

landing.farewell: Awa’difo amboni — thank you very much.
landing.audience: Complete beginners, families from West Nile, volunteers and travellers heading to Arua.
landing.first: Greetings, introductions and numbers, then family, food, the market, time, places, the home and health, unit by unit.

cast.emma: A visitor learning Lugbara before her trip
